---
title: "Wave-1 production publication"
description: "How Mail, Calendar, Apps, Finance and Drive publish to production: version upload, 0% staged smoke, traffic switch, health gate and automatic rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-25"
audience: developers
---

`wave1-native-production.yaml` publishes the wave-1 native Workers (Mail,
Calendar, Apps, Finance and Drive). The Production Deployment Planner calls it
through each app's `<app>-cloudflare.yaml` when a production push selects the
app; a dispatch of `wave1-native-production.yaml` from `production` is the only
manual route. A direct dispatch of `<app>-cloudflare.yaml` on `production`
never publishes: its run is not part of the upload history.

## Admission

- `productionPublicationPolicy` in `tuturuuu.ci.ts` admits the app. The caller's
  `production-policy` job, the called workflow's `production-policy` job and
  the publisher itself all check it.
- A called run defaults its `automatic` input to true, so an app with a
  `productionPublicationExemptions` record is held. Calendar has such a record
  until its first staged release by manual dispatch is smoked and serving;
  remove the record to let the planner publish it.
- A Worker that already serves through a Custom Domain or zone route publishes
  only when `productionServingTopology` records exactly that topology. Calendar's
  record is `calendar.tuturuuu.com` with no routes. Every other wave-1 Worker
  must stay route-free.

## Publish sequence

Everything below runs in the publish job. The preflight and verify steps hold
only the read token; the upload step holds only the deploy token and performs
every Cloudflare write.

1. **Read-only preflight.** Exact production SHA, topology, secrets, rollback
   deployment and upload history. The history walks manual dispatches and
   planner runs newest first. It skips attempts that provably never started an
   upload, receipts whose serving deployment was restored and confirmed, and
   superseded attempts. An `uncertain` or unknown attempt blocks. The serving
   SHA must be proven, from the serving version's annotation or from the
   accepted receipt that wrote it. When it is newer than the candidate, the
   attempt records `superseded` and uploads nothing.
2. **Version upload.** `cf workers versions create --prebuilt` creates the
   version with no traffic.
3. **Stage at 0%.** A gradual deployment keeps the serving version at 100% and
   adds the new version at 0%.
4. **Staged smoke.** Signed-out requests carry
   `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides: <worker>="<version>"`. The smoke
   contract:
   - `GET <public host>/api/build-info` and `GET tuturuuu.com/<mount>/api/build-info`
     answer 200 and report the candidate `commitHash`. Retries cover edge
     propagation for about a minute; if either path never reports it, the
     override did not reach the staged version and the smoke fails.
   - Where the app's source emits it (Finance today), `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native`
     must be present. Mail, Calendar, Apps and Drive do not emit it yet; their
     records keep the observed value. A test flips the requirement on when an
     app's `start-bridge.config.ts` starts emitting it.
   - `GET tuturuuu.com/<mount>` answers 307 into `https://tuturuuu.com/login`
     (Apps answers 200: its catalog is public; Drive has no apex mount).
   - Login pages answer without a 5xx, and the release recipe's smoke cases
     match.
   - Any 5xx or timeout fails the stage. Records keep each response's status
     and allowed headers (`cache-control`, `cf-ray`, `content-type`,
     `location`, `server`, `x-tuturuuu-runtime`), never a body.
5. **Abort or switch.** A failed smoke restores the serving deployment alone
   (`smoke-failed`); traffic never moves. Otherwise traffic switches to the
   new version at 100%, but only while the staged deployment is still active.
6. **Health gate.** Public probes without the override, every 10 seconds for
   about a minute: every build-info origin reports the candidate commit, and
   no probe answers 5xx or times out. On failure the upload step restores the
   recorded rollback deployment, confirms it is active, probes the restored
   state, records both outcomes (`rolled-back`) and fails the job. A restore
   that cannot be confirmed marks the receipt `uncertain` and the job fails
   loudly; restore the receipt's rollback deployment by hand.
7. **Verify.** The read-only step confirms the active version, script settings
   and unchanged topology, and records `accepted-private`.

The receipt artifact `wave1-<app>-production-publication-<sha>-<run>-<attempt>`
is retained 90 days in every outcome. An attempt that failed after its version
upload leaves that version in the Worker's history, so a rerun of the same SHA
refuses; ship a fix on a new SHA.

## Why a 0% gradual deployment

Cloudflare's version override header selects only among the versions of the
current deployment. Staging the new version at 0% beside the serving one puts
it in the current deployment, so the header reaches it on the app's real
public paths, with the Worker's real bindings and secrets, while no reader is
served by it. It changes no route, Custom Domain, `workers.dev` or preview URL
setting.

A preview-URL window would need `preview_urls` enabled on a production Worker:
a settings write that exposes every version on `workers.dev` until it is
reverted, outside the Access and gateway paths real users take. A failed revert
leaves that exposure open. The 0% deployment avoids both. The header is not
guaranteed to pass through every service binding, so the smoke fails closed
unless build-info on each path proves it reached the staged version.

## Concurrency

Builds of one app and SHA share a queue (`wave1-native-production-<app>-<sha>`);
uploads of one app share another (`wave1-native-upload-<app>`). Neither cancels
a run. Callers use a group per run on `production`, so no planner callee
replaces another.

- `scripts/ci/wave1-native-production-history.test.mjs`: upload history.
